<span id="top"></span>

A **vision foundation model** is an image encoder pretrained on a large image collection and reused for later tasks. Vision Transformers divide an image into patches and learn a feature vector for each patch. Self-supervised models such as DINO learn these features without class labels.

Students do not train a foundation model from scratch. In industrial anomaly detection, a frozen encoder can compare a test image with known normal images and identify unusual patches. An adapter can instead modify the encoder using the available normal images and deliberately generated synthetic defects.

The evaluation must keep the anomaly-detection protocol fixed. MVTec training sets contain normal images only; real test defects cannot be used to train or tune the model. Frozen features, parameter-efficient adaptation and full fine-tuning are comparable only when they use the same training information and objective.

::: {.category-callout}
**Three ways to adapt a pretrained backbone**

**Freeze it** and score distances from normal reference patches. **Adapt it efficiently** by training small LoRA or adapter modules. **Fine-tune it** by updating the complete encoder. Adaptation requires a stated objective; in this project it uses normal images and synthetic corruptions, not real test defects.
:::

## Learn first and find ideas

- Core reading: [DINO](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.14294), [DINOv2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.07193), the [DINOv2 model card and code](https://github.com/facebookresearch/dinov2), and [AnomalyDINO](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.14529) with its [official code](https://github.com/dammsi/AnomalyDINO).
- Parameter-efficient adaptation: [LoRA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685) and the [Hugging Face PEFT library](https://github.com/huggingface/peft).
- Synthetic-defect training: [CutPaste](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.04015) and [DRAEM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.07610) with its [official code](https://github.com/VitjanZ/DRAEM).
- Data and model hubs: [MVTec AD](https://www.mvtec.com/research-teaching/datasets/mvtec-ad), [Hugging Face models](https://huggingface.co/models) and [timm](https://github.com/huggingface/pytorch-image-models).
- Keep zero-shot, one-shot, few-shot and full-shot anomaly results separate, and never compare an image-level metric directly with a pixel-level metric.

## 3.1  Adapting DINO backbones for industrial anomaly detection {#project-3-1}

::: {.project-meta}
<span class="meta-label">Task</span><span class="meta-value">Image-level anomaly detection and pixel-level anomaly localisation</span>
<span class="meta-label">Level</span><span class="meta-value">BSc or MSc</span>
<span class="meta-label">Compute</span><span class="meta-value">Light for frozen features; moderate for adaptation (12–24 GB GPU recommended)</span>
<span class="meta-label">Data</span><span class="meta-value">[MVTec AD](https://www.mvtec.com/research-teaching/datasets/mvtec-ad) — 5,354 images, 15 categories, pixel-precise masks, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0</span>
<span class="meta-label">Starting paper</span><span class="meta-value">Oquab et al., [DINOv2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.07193), 2023</span>
:::

::: {.project-intro}
**What you will do.** Use DINOv2 patch features to detect and locate defects from normal reference images. The BSc project studies the frozen detector. The MSc project tests adaptation using normal images and synthetic defects.
:::

**Data.** [MVTec AD](https://www.mvtec.com/research-teaching/datasets/mvtec-ad) contains 5,354 images in 15 categories, with defect-free training images and labelled normal and defective test images. [MVTec AD 2](https://www.mvtec.com/research-teaching/datasets/mvtec-ad-2) contains 8,000+ images in eight harder scenarios and includes unseen lighting conditions. Both use CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; MVTec AD 2 also has a private-test evaluation server.

**Methods and code.** Use DINOv2 **ViT-S/14** from the [Apache-2.0 repository](https://github.com/facebookresearch/dinov2). The frozen route follows [AnomalyDINO](https://github.com/dammsi/AnomalyDINO): store normal patch features and score each test patch by its distance to the memory bank. The MSc route trains LoRA or adapters with [PEFT](https://github.com/huggingface/peft), using only normal training images and synthetic corruptions. Larger backbones are optional, not required.

**Baselines and evaluation.** Compare frozen AnomalyDINO with [PatchCore](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.08265). For the MSc route, compare frozen DINOv2, LoRA/adapter adaptation and full fine-tuning under the same synthetic-defect objective. Report image AUROC, pixel AUROC and the official AU-PRO measure per category, plus trainable parameters, memory and runtime. Keep shot count and public/private test protocols separate.

::: {.scope .scope-bsc}
**Bachelor research question.** **How do the number of normal reference images and the selected DINOv2 feature layer affect defect detection and localisation?**

*Core experiment.* Reproduce AnomalyDINO on MVTec AD with ViT-S/14. Compare 1, 4 and 16 normal reference images, two feature layers selected in advance, and PatchCore. Repeat the reference-image sampling and analyse false positives and localisation errors. No model training is required.
:::

::: {.scope .scope-msc}
**Master research question.** **Can parameter-efficient adaptation using only normal images and synthetic defects improve detection of real, unseen defects without reducing robustness to lighting changes?** Define one synthetic-defect generator and one feature-consistency or segmentation objective. Compare frozen DINOv2, LoRA/adapter adaptation and full fine-tuning with identical data and losses on MVTec AD and MVTec AD 2. Ablate the adapter depth and synthetic-defect generator.

The contribution is the adaptation and its controlled evaluation. Training on real test defects, or tuning choices repeatedly on the public test labels, would invalidate the unsupervised setting.
:::

**Practical notes.** DINOv2 code and standard weights are ungated and Apache 2.0. MVTec data is restricted to non-commercial use. Complete the BSc frozen baseline before beginning any adaptation.
